title: arXiv Physics — Friday, 2 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart. Ordering is inferred from concrete scientific results and methods, cross-listing, collaboration/publication status, and available artifacts. Citation evidence is limited for these new papers; this is not a readership or download ranking.

sections.title: Search for dark matter produced in association with a low-multiplicity jet in proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s) = 13 TeV
sections.abstract: CMS presents its first LHC search using a low-multiplicity jet plus missing transverse momentum, finding no excess and setting limits on vector- and axial-vector-mediator dark-matter models.
sections.claimed_result: CMS reports no excess; for dark-matter masses near 150 (550) GeV, mediator masses up to 4250 (3500) GeV are excluded at 95% CL in the stated simplified models.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; 2016–2018, 13 TeV CMS proton-proton data, supervised machine learning, and simulated samples.
sections.unique_caveat: The limits depend on the simplified vector/axial-vector mediator models and do not establish or exclude dark matter generically.

sections.title: Search for charged-lepton-flavour violating eμtq interactions at sqrt(s)=13 TeV with the ATLAS detector
sections.abstract: ATLAS searches for charged-lepton-flavour violation in top-quark production and decay using three-electron/muon final states, observes no significant deviation, and constrains six effective-field-theory coefficients.
sections.claimed_result: The authors set 95% CL limits on six EFT coefficients and report branching-ratio limits from B(t → eμu) < 6×10⁻⁹ to B(t → eμc) < 2.7×10⁻⁷ for the specified couplings.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; 140 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV proton-proton collision data recorded by ATLAS.
sections.unique_caveat: The limits are interpreted within an EFT framework and apply to the analyzed top-quark channels and dataset; no signal is observed.

sections.title: Drell-Yan lepton pair production from low to high transverse momentum
sections.abstract: The authors combine high-order perturbative predictions across transverse-momentum regimes, a Collins–Soper kernel from continuum-limit lattice QCD, and a maximum-entropy construction of positive event weights.
sections.claimed_result: The paper presents a particle-level calculation with N³LO and approximate N⁴LL′ accuracy at low/moderate transverse momentum, with stated extensions to multijet and high-momentum regimes, and strictly positive event weights.
sections.evidence_type: Computational/theoretical; perturbative QCD predictions with a nonperturbative Collins–Soper input from continuum-limit lattice QCD.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated accuracies are regime-dependent and include approximate higher-order terms; the method relies on the lattice-derived kernel.

sections.title: Thermal axion production in QCD from the lattice
sections.abstract: Neubauer and Moore show how Euclidean lattice-QCD correlators can yield weighted integrals of the axion production spectrum without analytic continuation, and demonstrate feasibility in pure-glue QCD at 1.5 Tc.
sections.claimed_result: Their test extracts the n=0 and n=1 weighted integrals with good signal-to-noise and finds the n=2 integral feasible with marginal signal-to-noise.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; finite-temperature pure-glue lattice-QCD calculations at one temperature, T = 1.5 Tc.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a pure-glue proof of principle at a single lattice spacing and temperature, not a full-QCD determination of the momentum-resolved production rate.

sections.title: Magnetic Phase Diagrams and Spin Hamiltonian of Monoclinic alpha-RuCl3 from Angle-Dependent Torque Studies
sections.abstract: Torque measurements on small monoclinic α-RuCl3 crystals map field-angle-dependent magnetic phases and show differences from larger rhombohedral samples, compared with mean-field spin-Hamiltonian calculations.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report reduced rotational symmetry, higher fields needed to suppress magnetic order, and distinct field-induced phases in small crystals that remain monoclinic.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental with theoretical comparison; piezo-cantilever torque measurements on sub-100 μm crystals and mean-field calculations.
sections.unique_caveat: The samples are unusually small; size- or strain-related suppression of the structural transition is discussed as a possible explanation, and minimal models are not a unique microscopic identification.

sections.title: A New Framework for Modeling Solar Flares from MHD to Kinetic Processes
sections.abstract: Allred and colleagues link magnetohydrodynamic flare evolution, kinetic particle acceleration, and particle transport/atmospheric radiation in a coupled simulation framework.
sections.claimed_result: The modeled white-light flare emission height is consistent with observations, according to the authors; this is a simulation result, not a new observation.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; a 2.5D ARMS MHD simulation coupled to kinetic particle distributions and RADYN+FP atmospheric modeling.
sections.unique_caveat: The framework is not yet fully three-dimensional, which the authors describe as future work.

sections.title: Analytic Metric for Rotating Black Holes in Higher-Derivative Gravity
sections.abstract: Hu, Li, and Yunes introduce an analytic metric-reconstruction method and construct a rotating black-hole metric in parity-even cubic gravity at linear order in the coupling, without spin or weak-field expansions.
sections.claimed_result: The paper presents the first analytic spinning black-hole metric in the specified cubic-gravity setting and coupling order.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical/computational; analytic metric reconstruction with field-equation and horizon-property checks.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is perturbative in the higher-derivative coupling; the abstract does not claim a nonperturbative solution or an observational test.

sections.title: Single-Particle Spectral Estimation
sections.abstract: Chapman and colleagues formulate Hamiltonian learning for a hidden non-interacting sector, prove the task DQC1-hard, and propose SPICES to estimate its spectral distribution under stated assumptions.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim efficient recovery in Wasserstein distance under natural assumptions, without reconstructing the unknown global unitary.
sections.evidence_type: Theoretical/computational; quantum-algorithm analysis and classical postprocessing, with no experimental demonstration reported in the abstract.
sections.unique_caveat: The efficiency guarantee is conditional on the paper’s assumptions; hardware noise and practical resource performance are not established by the abstract.
